args.body:
PRIVILEGED AND CONFIDENTIAL — ATTORNEY WORK PRODUCT
REDLINE REVIEW MEMORANDUM

To:      Transaction Team
From:    Funds & Asset Management Group
Date:    [Matter Date]
Re:      Redline Review of Investment Advisory Agreement — Counterparty Markup Analysis Against Standard Form and Internal Playbook

------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
I.  INTRODUCTION, SCOPE, AND GOVERNING INSTRUCTIONS
------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

This memorandum presents a comprehensive redline review of the counterparty's markup of the
Investment Advisory Agreement (the "Agreement") against the firm's standard form and the
applicable internal playbook, reconciled with the operative engagement materials for this
funds asset management matter. The deliverable analyzes each deviation introduced by the
counterparty markup, reconciles those deviations against the disclosure schedules and
exhibits, and recommends an accept/reject/counter position, all in accordance with the
controlling instructions from the deal team.

Governing Materials Reviewed (in full):
  (a)  Engagement input materials for this funds asset management matter (the standard-form
       baseline and internal playbook position the counterparty markup was measured against).
  (b)  The counterparty markup, which "accepts most firm-standard provisions" but introduces
       defined deviations that this memo flags, analyzes, and reconciles.
  (c)  The schedules and exhibits (Schedules 3.7 and 5.2; Exhibit B), which qualify the base
       materials and narrow the very representations the markup also touches.
  (d)  The deal team correspondence, the latest message of which sets the controlling
       negotiation priorities and supersedes all earlier, contrary messages in the thread.

Materials Excluded as Not Reliable:
  The matter folder also contained an administrative correspondence file that was misfiled
  into this matter. That file concerns a different client engagement and is explicitly flagged
  in the folder as unrelated. It has been reviewed and excluded in full and is not relied upon
  anywhere in this analysis. No inference in this memo draws from that file.

Controlling Deal Direction (from the latest deal team message):
  The client WILL CONCEDE the counterparty's conversion of the indemnification basket from a
  deductible to a tipping basket.
  The client TREATS ANY REDUCTION OF THE SURVIVAL PERIOD as a walk-away issue.
  (Superseded earlier messages stated the reverse priority ordering; only the latest message
  controls and is reflected below.)

------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
II.  EXECUTIVE SUMMARY OF DEVIATIONS AND RECOMMENDED POSITIONS
------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

The counterparty markup accepts most firm-standard provisions but introduces three material
deviations. Each is classified below; detailed analysis follows in Section IV.

  Deviation 1 — Indemnification cap reduced and indemnification basket converted from a
                deductible to a tipping basket (Indemnification provision).
                Disposition: PARTIALLY ACCEPT / COUNTER. The basket conversion is CONCEDED per
                controlling deal instruction; the cap reduction is NOT accepted.

  Deviation 2 — Material Adverse Effect (MAE) definition amended to add carve-outs for
                regulatory action "of exactly the kind at issue in this matter."
                Disposition: REJECT / COUNTER. The carve-outs conflict with Schedule 3.7, which
                discloses two pending regulatory inquiries that the carve-outs would sweep out
                of the definition of MAE.

  Deviation 3 — New limitation period shortening the survival of the core representations
                (Survival / Limitation Period).
                Disposition: REJECT — WALK-AWAY ISSUE. Any survival-period reduction is a
                walk-away item under the controlling deal instruction. The proposed change also
                directly contradicts Exhibit B's survival matrix.

------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
III.  RECONCILIATION FRAMEWORK — ORDER OF AUTHORITY
------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

Consistent with the operative materials, the reconciliation hierarchy for this engagement is:

   1.  Controlling deal team instruction (latest message) — governs negotiation priorities and
       walk-away red lines.
   2.  Schedules and exhibits — scheduled exceptions CONTROL over general statements in the
       base materials. Schedule 3.7, Schedule 5.2, and Exhibit B qualify the counterparty
       markup's touched provisions and therefore govern interpretation of those provisions.
   3.  Counterparty markup — analyzed as the source of the deviations.
   4.  Standard-form / internal playbook baseline — the benchmark against which deviations are
       measured.

The deliverables in this matter must reconcile the counterparty markup AND the schedules/
exhibits against the base materials, giving the scheduled exceptions controlling weight.

------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
IV.  DEVIATION-BY-DEVIATION ANALYSIS
------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

(a) Deviation 1 — Indemnification Cap Reduction and Basket Conversion

    Counterparty Proposal. The counterparty's markup (i) silently reduces the indemnification
    cap and (ii) converts the indemnification basket from a true deductible to a tipping
    basket.

    Reconciliation Against Base Materials and Schedules.
      - Basket conversion. The standard form contemplates a deductible structure, under which
        the indemnitor bears losses only above the basket threshold. A "tipping" basket
        instead shifts the entire liability (including the first-dollar amount) once the
        threshold is crossed, materially increasing the indemnitor's exposure profile once
        triggered.
      - Cap reduction. The standard form establishes a firm-standard indemnification cap. The
        markup's silent reduction lowers the ceiling on recoverable indemnity without
        corresponding consideration.
      - Schedule 5.2. This schedule lists retained liabilities that the markup's indemnification
        changes would silently shift. Any reduction of the cap or recharacterization of the
        basket must be tested against the Schedule 5.2 retained-liability schedule, because the
        scheduled exceptions narrow the scope of what is indemnifiable and would interact with
        a lower cap or a tipping basket to compound or diminish recovery depending on which
        retained liabilities are excluded.

    Application of Controlling Deal Direction.
      - The latest deal team message concedes the basket conversion (the tipping basket).
        Accordingly, we RECOMMEND ACCEPTING the conversion of the basket from a deductible to
        a tipping basket, as directed, without further negotiation on that specific point.
      - The cap reduction is a separate and independent change. The controlling instruction
        concedes the basket conversion only. It does not authorize any reduction of the
        indemnification cap. The firm-standard cap should be preserved.

    Recommended Position.
      - ACCEPT the basket conversion (per controlling instruction).
      - COUNTER/REJECT the indemnification cap reduction; revert to the standard-form cap.
        Confirm that Schedule 5.2 retained-liability exception continues to tie into the
        standard cap and is not overridden by the markup.

(b) Deviation 2 — MAE Definition Carve-Outs for Regulatory Action

    Counterparty Proposal. The markup amends the definition of Material Adverse Effect to add
    carve-outs for "regulatory action" — specifically carve-outs designed to remove regulatory
    action from the MAE definition.

    Reconciliation Against Base Materials and Schedules.
      - Schedule 3.7 discloses TWO PENDING REGULATORY INQUIRIES that intersect the MAE
        carve-outs the markup introduces. The markup's carve-outs are expressly "of exactly the
        kind at issue in this matter" — i.e., they are drafted to carve out the very regulatory
        matters that Schedule 3.7 discloses.
      - If accepted, the carve-outs would exclude these two pending regulatory inquiries from
        being treated as a Material Adverse Effect, thereby removing a basis for the client to
        invoke MAE protections with respect to those disclosed regulatory matters.
      - Because Schedule 3.7 is a scheduled exception that specifically discloses these two
        inquiries, and the schedules control over general statements in the base materials, the
        markup's general carve-out language must be read against the disclosed inquiries.
        Adopting the carve-outs without a corresponding Schedule 3.7 qualification would create
        an internally inconsistent position: the schedule discloses the inquiries, while the
        MAE definition would strip the client of MAE recourse for exactly those inquiries.

    Recommended Position.
      - REJECT / COUNTER the MAE carve-outs as drafted. If the counterparty persists on the
        concept, the carve-outs must be narrowed so that they do not apply to the two pending
        regulatory inquiries disclosed on Schedule 3.7, or the Schedule must be amended to
        carve out those inquiries from the operation of the new MAE qualification. At minimum,
        the client must retain the ability to treat the disclosed regulatory inquiries as a
        Material Adverse Effect where they have a material adverse impact on the business,
        financial condition, or results of operations.

(c) Deviation 3 — Reduction of Survival Period for Core Representations

    Counterparty Proposal. The markup introduces a new limitation period that SHORTENS the
    survival of the core representations.

    Reconciliation Against Base Materials and Schedules.
      - Exhibit B sets the survival matrix for the Agreement, establishing the survival windows
        for each class of representation (including the core representations). The markup's
        proposed shorter limitation period CONTRADICTS Exhibit B's survival matrix.
      - Because Exhibit B supplies the controlling survival matrix for the transaction, the
        markup's conflicting limitation period cannot both govern. The scheduled exhibit must
        control.
      - Absent a conforming amendment to Exhibit B, the markup creates a direct conflict between
        the body-of-agreement limitation provision and the exhibit. That conflict should be
        resolved in favor of the survival matrix set forth on Exhibit B.

    Application of Controlling Deal Direction.
      - The controlling deal team instruction treats ANY reduction of the survival period as a
        WALK-AWAY ISSUE. This is the highest-priority, non-concessional red line in the
        negotiation.
      - The proposed limitation period is a direct survival-period reduction and, therefore,
        triggers the walk-away instruction.

    Recommended Position.
      - REJECT the survival-period reduction outright. Under the controlling instruction, this
        is a walk-away issue: the firm should not accept any shortening of the survival of the
        core representations, and if the counterparty persists, the client is prepared to walk
        away from the transaction on this ground.
      - Revert the limitation period to the survival matrix set forth on Exhibit B, which
        reflects the standard-form/playbook position for the core representations.

------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
V.  INTERACTION AND NET RISK ASSESSMENT
------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

Viewed together, the three deviations reflect a coordinated effort by the counterparty to
narrow the client's protection on three fronts simultaneously:
      (1)  lowering the ceiling on recovery (indemnification cap),
      (2)  narrowing the trigger for MAE-based relief on the very regulatory risks disclosed on
           Schedule 3.7 (MAE carve-outs), and
      (3)  compressing the window within which the client may pursue claims (survival period).

Even though the client will concede the basket conversion, the combination of a reduced cap,
an MAE carve-out tied to the disclosed regulatory inquiries, and a shortened survival period
would, taken together, materially erode the client's post-closing remedies. The undisclosed
cap reduction and the survival-period reduction in particular represent clear deviations from
the standard form that must be remediated.

------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
VI.  RECOMMENDATIONS AND NEXT STEPS
------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

  1.  Indemnification basket — accept the conversion to a tipping basket, consistent with the
      controlling deal instruction and the Schedule 5.2 review.
  2.  Indemnification cap — reject the silent reduction; reinstate the standard-form cap. Ensure
      Schedule 5.2 retained-liability schedule remains consistent with the standard cap.
  3.  MAE carve-outs — reject the regulatory-action carve-outs as drafted; amend the definition
      (and/or Schedule 3.7) so that the two pending regulatory inquiries disclosed on Schedule
      3.7 are not excluded from MAE. Retain the client's ability to invoke MAE for material
      adverse effects arising from those inquiries.
  4.  Survival period — reject any reduction; reaffirm the Exhibit B survival matrix. Treat any
      survival-period reduction as a walk-away issue per the controlling deal direction.
  5.  Prior to execution, confirm that (i) the final agreement resolves the conflict between any
      body-of-agreement limitation provision and Exhibit B in favor of the exhibit, and
      (ii) all three deviations are reconciled against Schedules 3.7 and 5.2 and Exhibit B so the
      scheduled exceptions control over any general statements.

------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
VII.  CONCLUSION
------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

The counterparty markup is largely consistent with the standard form but introduces three
material deviations. Following the controlling deal direction, the firm should accept the
indemnification basket conversion, reject the indemnification cap reduction, reject the MAE
regulatory-action carve-outs (or narrow them so the Schedule 3.7 disclosures remain covered),
and reject any survival-period reduction as a walk-away issue. The deliverable has reconciled
the counterparty markup against the schedules/exhibits and the base materials, giving
controlling weight to the latest deal team instruction and the scheduled exceptions as required.

This memorandum is privileged and confidential attorney work product prepared in anticipation
of litigation and negotiation and is not for distribution outside the legal and deal teams
without authorization.

------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
                    END OF REDLINE REVIEW MEMORANDUM
------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
